ordinary writing

</button>
</h4>
<p>

Learner priority
</h3>

1
</span>

</h4>
<p>
hear first; learn with word
</p>
</article>
<article class="chart-tile pitch-advice-row">
<span class="chart-label pitch-rank">
2
</span>
<h4 class="chart-label">
vowel length
</h4>
<p>
short vs long changes rhythm
</p>
</article>
<article class="chart-tile pitch-advice-row">
<span class="chart-label pitch-rank">
3
</span>
<h4 class="chart-label">
pitch contour

?
</button>
</h4>
<p>
dialect-sensitive; dictionary mark helps
</p>
</article>
</div>

<section class="chart-group pitch-reading">
<header class="chart-group-head">
<h3>
Reading order
</h3>
</header>
<ol class="chart-tiles pitch-advice-list">
<li class="chart-tile pitch-advice-row">
<span class="chart-label pitch-rank">
1
</span>
<p>
Find marked syllable.
</p>
</li>
<li class="chart-tile pitch-advice-row">
<span class="chart-label pitch-rank">
2
</span>
<p>
Read length: short mark or long mark.
</p>
</li>
<li class="chart-tile pitch-advice-row">
<span class="chart-label pitch-rank">
3
</span>
<p>
Keep post-accent macrons long.
</p>
</li>
<li class="chart-tile pitch-advice-row">
<span class="chart-label pitch-rank">
4
</span>
<p>
Do not move stress to final syllable.
</p>
</li>
</ol>
</section>
### popover [data-pitch-note]|[["data-pitch-note","falling"]]
<article class="chart-tip">
<h4>
Falling accent
</h4>
<p>
Standard falling accents appear on one-syllable words or the first syllable of longer words.
</p>
</article>
### popover [data-pitch-note]|[["data-pitch-note","final"]]
<article class="chart-tip">
<h4>
Final stress
</h4>
<p>
Native standard words avoid final stress. Loans, names, and dialect forms can break the learner rule.
</p>
</article>
### popover [data-pitch-note]|[["data-pitch-note","length"]]
<article class="chart-tip">
<h4>
Post-accent length
</h4>
<p>
Macron marks long vowels without stress. In standard accent notation, these long vowels occur after the accented syllable.
</p>
</article>
### popover [data-pitch-note]|[["data-pitch-note","marks"]]
<article class="chart-tip">
<h4>
Marks are reference notation
</h4>
<p>
Books, dictionaries, and teaching material mark accent. Normal Serbian spelling does not.
</p>
</article>
### popover [data-pitch-note]|[["data-pitch-note","mobile"]]
<article class="chart-tip">
<h4>
Accent can move
</h4>
<p>
Case, number, and derivation can change stress place, tone, and length. Treat common paradigms as word facts.
</p>
</article>
### popover [data-pitch-note]|[["data-pitch-note","rising"]]
<article class="chart-tip">
<h4>
Rising accent
</h4>
<p>
The rise is heard across the stressed syllable and what follows. Do not turn it into English question intonation.
</p>
</article>
### popover [data-pitch-note]|[["data-pitch-note","urban"]]
<article class="chart-tip">
<h4>
Modern speech
</h4>
<p>
Many speakers keep stress place and length more clearly than the four-way pitch contrast, especially in urban speech.
</p>
</article>
